summary: Yaroslav Komarovski works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at multiple institutions, including the University of Virginia and Dzongsar Institute, under Jeffrey Hopkins and several traditional teachers. He was a Mellon fellow at Washington University and became Professor at University of Nebraska-Lincoln in 2009.

Yaroslav Vasilkov is an Indologist and historian. He earned his doctorate at Saint Petersburg State University (1961–1967). His career includes positions at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (~1967), Saint Petersburg State University, and Kunstkamera, where he became Chief Researcher in 2005.

Yashaswini Chandra specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She held positions at SOAS University of London (2011–2012), Jawaharlal Nehru University (2012–2013), and Sahapedia (2011–2018), and later served as Visiting Faculty at Ashoka University (2019) and at the University of Edinburgh (2023).

Yasuaki Nara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at the University of Calcutta. He was an instructor and later Professor Emeritus at Komazawa University and led the Soto Zen Research Center.

Yasuhiko Nagano is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1977–1983). He served as Professor and Professor Emeritus at the National Museum of Ethnology and held executive posts at SOKENDAI.
Yasuhiko Sueki specializes in philosophy and sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1971 to 1980 and became Professor Emeritus at Komazawa University around 2017.

Yasuhiro Okazaki specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and has held teaching posts at Chiyoda, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe, and Takamiya High Schools.

Yasuhiro Sueki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He undertook short-term study at the Tübingen University Library under George Baumann (~1985–1986) and held positions at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. By 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies and held a post at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004), and was attested as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University in 2004.

Yasuhiro Yamazaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koyasan University (~1950–1954). He served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1978–2000).

Yasuke Ikari is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Chicago (PhD) under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He served as an assistant and associate professor at Kyoto University, later becoming Professor Emeritus in 2004.

Yasuko Kojima specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Yasumasa Sekine is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at the Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. His academic appointments include positions at Gakushuin Women's Junior College, the University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

Yasunori Ejima was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his MA and doctorate at the University of Tokyo, where he later served as an assistant professor, associate professor, and full professor from 1987 to 1999.

Yasuo Deguchi is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He taught at Nagoya Institute of Technology before returning to Kyoto University, where he became Professor in 2016 and Dean of Letters in 2023.

Yasuo Goto is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a lecturer and part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1991 and 2006) and as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

Yasuo Inamoto is a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a technical official at the Nara National Museum from ~1996 to 2006 and held a post at Kyoto University around 2006.

Yasuo Matsunami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano, served there as a lecturer (attested 1992–2006), and was an advisor to the Śrāvakabhūmi Study Group until 2010.
Yasuo Sano is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.
